what: A cutout picture such as a car crosses its own band in a straight line (linear) and repeats endlessly — by default from -100% to 400% of its own width over 8s (a car slowly passing between sections). Swapping the start and end makes it go the other way: two taxis zipping along the road behind a big photo from 200% to -200% in 2.5s. Because start and end are multiples of its own width, it looks the same speed even if the image size changes

options.--fx-from: Start position (as style, % of its own width), default -100%
options.--fx-to: Arrival position (via style, % of own width), default 400% — taxi uses --fx-from: 200%; --fx-to: -200%
options.--fx-dur: Length of a single pass (via style), default 8s — taxi 2.5s
options.--fx-delay: Initial start delay (via style), default 0s — negative starts mid-motion
options.--fx-flip: -1 flips the picture left to right (via style), default 1 — so the front of a car heading the other way faces its direction of travel
options.--fx-rest: Position to stand at when reduced motion is set (via style), default 0%

use: ·
note: Put overflow: hidden (or clip) on the parent holding the strip so pictures that leave the screen do not cause horizontal overflow
